# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 78 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 78 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_078_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Chapter 1

**1** He showed me a great willow tree overshadowing plains and mountains, and under the shade of the willow had come all those who are called by the name of the Lord. **2** And an angel of the Lord, glorious and very tall, was standing beside the willow, holding a great sickle, and he was cutting branches from the willow and giving them to the people who were sheltered under the willow; and he gave them little rods, about a cubit in length. **3** After all had received the rods, the angel laid down his sickle, and that tree was sound, just as I had seen it before. **4** I marveled within myself, saying, "How is the tree sound after so many branches have been cut off?" The shepherd said to me, "Do not marvel that the tree remained sound after so many branches were cut off; wait until you see everything, and it will be shown to you what it is." **5** The angel who had given the rods to the people asked them back again; and in the order in which each one had received them, they were summoned to him, and each one gave back his rod. And the angel of the Lord took them and examined them. **6** From some he received the rods withered and moth-eaten; the angel ordered those who had given back rods in that state to stand apart. **7** Others gave back their rods withered, but not moth-eaten; and these also he ordered to stand apart. **8** Others gave back their rods half-withered; these also stood apart. **9** Others gave back their rods half-withered and cracked; these also stood apart. **10** Others gave back their rods green and cracked; these also stood apart. **11** Others gave back their rods half-green and half-withered; these also stood apart. **12** Others brought their rods two-thirds green and one-third withered; these also stood apart. **13** Others gave back their rods two-thirds withered and one-third green; these also stood apart. **14** Others gave back their rods nearly all green, with only a very little withered, just the tip; these stood apart. **15** The rods of still others were completely green; these stood apart, and the angel greatly rejoiced over them, and the shepherd also rejoiced over them.

---

*EMET renders all botanical and evaluative terms precisely. The willow (Greek itea) represents the Law of God or the Son of God in later exposition. "Rod" (rhabdos) maintained throughout.*
